answer_raw.explanation: After the maintenance shutdown, the replaced feed-water line fitting introduced a metal contaminant into the culture. This raised broth turbidity (the cloudier harvest noted in records) and suppressed product titer ~30%. Evidence: cutting feed-water flow to 0 raised titer from 23.6 to 64.9 and dropped turbidity ~42->5; adding a metal-chelating additive at 60 raised titer to ~63.8 while also dropping turbidity, directly reversing the effect and implicating a chelatable metal as the cause. The chelator dose-response is an inverted-U (dose 90 gave only 57.9, a downside from over-chelation stripping essential trace metals), with a fitted optimum near 71 and the dose grid peaking at 70. The operators' leading theories were wrong: DO control drift was ruled out, and temperature/DO are bystanders that do not drive titer. Decisive test: chelation reversed the titer loss without changing feed flow, isolating a chelatable metal as the causal agent rather than DO or temperature. Recommended fix: dose the metal-chelating additive at ~70 (and/or inspect/replace the feed-water fitting to remove the source).
